newsitem.title: MALTA: Mid-Med shares shed three cents as BoV bank gains.
newsitem.headline: Mid-Med shares shed three cents as BoV bank gains.

text.p: The share index dropped 1.21 point in Wednesday's trading session of the Malta Stock Exchange as average Mid-Med Bank share prices shed three cents and Farsons ordinary lost one cent.
Bank of Valletta (BoV) shares gained two cents in the last cum-div trading following the announcement of annual results last week.

Turnover in the once-weekly trading session reached Lm432,200 ($1.2 million) from just over Lm145,670 ($404,962) last week. There were 113 deals, of which 69 were in equities and 44 in fixed income securities.

Business in equities amounted to just over Lm126,200 with 93,457 shares transacted. Of these, 71,157 were Bank of Valletta shares transacted in 58 deals for an average of 133 cents per share, up two cents.
There were four deals in Mid-Med Bank, with 13,800 shares being transacted for an average 150 cents per share, down three cents.
In Lombard Bank Malta, 6,000 shares changed hands for an average 151 cents per share, up three mils.

A total of 2,000 Farsons ordinary shares sold for an average 51 cents per share, down one cent. In the Farsons 8.5 percent preference shares 1996/99, 500 shares were negotiated at an average price of 100.1 cents.
In the government bond market, 14 issues were dealt in, turnover reaching 296,100. Business was mainly in he seven percent MGS 2006 and the 7.5 percent MGS 2011, in which there were two block trades.
There was one deal in the 6.5 percent Gasan Bonds 1998/99 amounting to Lm9,850. (One Lm=$2.78)
